newsitem.title: DUBAI: Oman plans aluminium smelter, aided by gas.
newsitem.headline: Oman plans aluminium smelter, aided by gas.

text.p: Banking on Oman's abundant gas reserves, a group of international companies is planning to develop what will be one of the Middle East's largest aluminium smelters, an Omani official said on Tuesday.

"The aluminium smelter is not a stand-alone project. It is related to the petrochemical project. We have a lot of gas," said Oman Ministry of Commerce and Industry undersecretary Ali Masoud al-Sunaidy.

"It is a proposal to the Omani government. It should reach 480,000 tonnes a year by the year 2003 and the investment is estimated at $2.4 billion," he said of the plans for the smelter in the industrial port city of Sohar in northern Oman.
Sunaidi said a proposal had also been put forward to the government for a 450,000 tonnes a year polyethylene plant.

As part of its drive to diversify the economy away from dependence on the 850,000 barrels of oil it pumps daily, Oman is setting up a $6 billion project to produce 6.6 million tonnes a year of liquefied natural gas from the year 2000.

Power for smelting is one of the biggest costs of aluminium production. Last month Dubai Aluminium (Dubal) chief executive Ian Rugeroni said that for this reason, and geographical location, the Gulf would develop into a leading source of aluminium.

Sunaidy said Hong Kong-based Charus Enterprises, Kaiser Aluminum Corp of the United States, British power generator National Power Plc and China Non-Ferrous Metals Co were awaiting Oman's approval for the smelter.
"They have given the bid to the government and are waiting for the okay," Sunaidy said, adding that this was likely within about the next two months.

It had been proposed that the plant, which would take around two years to complete, would be 75 percent financed by borrowings and 25 percent by equity, split between Omani private companies and the foreign partners, he said.
Most of the raw materials for the production of aluminium would have to be imported. "That is why we see this combination of companies," Sunaidy said.

Apart from Dubal, the Gulf is home to another smelter, Aluminium Bahrain -- currently the Middle East's biggest producer -- with capacity of 460,000 tonnes. It has plans to add another 36,500 tonnes by May 1997.
Dubal is in the process of expanding capacity, by over 50 percent to 375,000 tonnes a year.
